name: CA-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Post-redistricting district leans Democratic by 7 points on the partisan index
Polymarket prices a Democratic win at 96%
Mike McGuire has outraised incumbent James Gallagher and enjoys outside support
Gallagher's incumbency is the main Republican asset, worth only a modest offset
model.rationale: The redrawn CA-01 sits well to the left of its old configuration, and markets price McGuire as a heavy favorite despite Gallagher's incumbency. McGuire's fundraising edge and outside backing reinforce a fundamentals-driven Democratic advantage of roughly 17 points.
model.watch: Any credible general-election polling showing Gallagher competitive, or a surge of Republican outside spending, would be the first sign the race is tightening.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; fundamentals point clearly one way (post-redistricting), so it is treated as safe for that party.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
California's 1st District was redrawn to favor Democrats, with a partisan index about seven points Democratic, and incumbent Republican James Gallagher now faces state Senator Mike McGuire in a district that no longer resembles the one he first won. McGuire has raised more money than Gallagher, about 2.3 million dollars to just under 2 million, and has outside group support while Gallagher holds a larger cash-on-hand balance. No public general-election polling is available, and no expert raters have published ratings for the race.

Prediction markets price a Democratic win at roughly 96 percent, consistent with the fundamentals-based view that the new district lines and a favorable national environment outweigh Gallagher's incumbency advantage. The race is rated Safe Democratic, with the main uncertainty coming from the absence of polling rather than any specific contrary evidence.
